title: The Mouse Deer and the Crocodile
summary: The little mouse deer must cross a river full of hungry crocodiles to reach a garden of ripe fruit. How will it do it?
moral: A clever mind is worth more than strength. But use your cleverness wisely!
pages: In the middle of a leafy forest lived a small, very clever mouse deer. That morning the sun shone warmly and the birds sang, but the mouse deer's stomach rumbled: grumble, grumble! 'Oh, I am so hungry,' it said.

From a distance, the mouse deer saw a garden across the river. The mango and guava trees were full of ripe fruit! Sadly, the river was home to many hungry crocodiles whose eyes peeped out from the water. 'How can I cross?' the mouse deer murmured.

Suddenly the mouse deer smiled. It had an idea! 'Hey, brave crocodiles!' it called. 'The King of the Forest is holding a feast of meat, and I have been told to count all of you who are invited!' The crocodiles looked at one another and emerged from the water.
'Line up from this bank to the other, so I can count you easily!' said the mouse deer. The greedy crocodiles hurried to line up closely, imagining the delicious meat at the feast.

Hop! The mouse deer leapt onto the first crocodile's back. 'One!' Hop! Onto the second crocodile's back. 'Two!' Hop! Onto the third crocodile's back. 'Three!' It counted while leaping nimbly to the other side.

The mouse deer reached the other side! With one last leap, it landed on the grassy riverbank. 'Thank you, crocodiles! I just wanted to cross; there is no feast of meat!' it called, laughing cheerfully.
The crocodiles gaped, then growled in anger. 'We have been tricked!' But it was too late. The mouse deer was already far away and out of reach, while they could only grumble in the water.

In the garden, the mouse deer ate mangoes and guavas until it was full. That day it learned, and so do we: cleverness can help us out of danger. But we should use it for good, not to deceive. The end.
